sources.quote: If the reporting deadline falls on a weekend or holiday, when is the report due? The report is due the following business day. For example, if March 1st falls on a Sunday, reports will be due on Monday, March 2nd.

value.basis: 0.5% per month on outstanding unpaid amounts from the due date until paid, capped at 50% of the amount due; separate late-filing penalty (5%/month up to 50%, or $100/day up to $5,000) and late-payment penalty (0.5%/month up to 25%); 75% fraud penalty

sources.quote: Interest at 0.5% per month on outstanding unpaid amounts accrues from the date the amounts or property were due under this chapter until paid. Interest due in accordance with this subsection may not exceed 50% of the amount required to be paid.

interest.todo: Statute states a MONTHLY rate (0.5%/month); annualRatePct 6 is 0.5 x 12 for the engine's shape - compute monthly. Waivable for good cause (§ 1185). Handbook p.49 notes current policy not to impose interest/penalties on voluntary late reports.

notes: Single annual report with contemporaneous remittance (not two-stage).

Several Ch. 11 sections carry notes 'For application of this section, see 84 Del. Laws, c. 368' (incl. §§ 1130, 1144, 1150) - a recent session law with application/effective-date provisions that were NOT reviewed. Human should check 84 Del. Laws c. 368 § 16-17 before relying on § 1144 dates.
Records retention: 10 years after the report was filed (§ 1145).

Handbook used: Delaware Holder Handbook, AUGUST 2026, VERSION 1 (64 pp), downloaded from unclaimedproperty.delaware.gov/docs/DE_Holder_Handbook.pdf; NAUPA's page still links a 2024 manual URL that now serves the SPA shell.
Negative reports are not required for ordinary holders (Handbook p.11), except post-SOS-VDA.

2026.10.1-draft (2026-10-29): businessDayRollForward filled from the DE OUP holder FAQ (unverified). Delaware interest stays a MONTHLY rate (0.5%/mo); the audit-interest meter does not approximate it as an annual rate, so DE interest shows UNKNOWN by design.
